grade_reason: Blocked from here: the agency's site refused this machine (HTTP 403 on a HEAD and on a page fetch), so no data file could be read and the key Well Permits file's columns are unknown. Content looks better than D: the agency lists free downloads (Well Permits, Pending Well Permits, Well Spots, Directional Well Data) and a legacy map service has a spud date (wells) and a received date (pending permits). Provisional: B at best from what was read (spud dates; filing dates for pending permits only), A only if the Well Permits file has an approval date and answers from a runner.
producer_plan: Nothing buildable from what was verified. Step 1, from the machine that will run the producer (the GitHub runner), make one HEAD or one ?f=json request each to: the agency downloads page and its zipped Well Permits and Pending Well Permits files; the ECMC Wells service on the state DNR GIS server; and the two legacy DNR services read here. Record the status; do not retry a refusal. Step 2, if the Well Permits file answers, read its column names and look for an approval or issue date, a permit type and a document number; if it has them, monthly approved permits by type is a filter and a count (grade A). Step 3, if only the map services answer: spuds by month from Spud_Date in the wells layer (point per well, Stat_Date is the last status change, a snapshot not a history), and filing dates only for permits still pending (receive_date in the pending layer; permits leave it once approved, so it cannot give a monthly history unless captured often and kept). Note Colorado also permits multi-well development plans, so a count of wells may not equal a count of Form 2 permits. Work types may come from permit_type (2-letter codes, meaning not verified) or from COGIS record pages (one well at a time, not bulk).
privacy_notes: The two legacy layers read hold operator numbers and company names and well names only; I saw no individual's name, but an operator can be a person, so apply the project's name rule. The agency's download page names GIS staff contacts (not copied). Form 2 was not read, so whether it asks for surface or mineral owner details is unknown.
